question: Explain the difference between depth-first search (DFS) and breadth-first search (BFS) for graph traversal. When would you choose one over the other?

keyPoints: DFS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, uses stack (recursive or explicit)
BFS explores all neighbors at current depth before moving deeper, uses queue
BFS finds shortest path in unweighted graphs, DFS uses less memory for deep graphs
DFS better for topological sorting, cycle detection; BFS better for shortest paths
expectedAnswer.explanation: DFS and BFS represent fundamentally different exploration strategies. DFS goes deep first, making it ideal for problems requiring complete path exploration like maze solving or topological sorting. BFS explores level by level, guaranteeing shortest paths in unweighted graphs, making it ideal for finding minimum distances or connection degrees.
